heroHeadline: SpaceX Files IPO S-1: $18.7B Revenue, 10.3M Starlink Subscribers — IFT-12 Block 3 Starship NET Tonight at 22:30 UTC
heroSubtitle: 8,781 days of SpaceX milestones — On May 20, 2026, SpaceX filed its public S-1 registration statement with the SEC (EDGAR 000162828026036936), marking the company's historic transition from 24 years of private operation to a planned Nasdaq IPO (ticker: SPCX). Key S-1 disclosures: 2025 revenue $18.7 billion (+33% YoY), 2025 net loss $4.94 billion, Q1 2026 revenue $4.69 billion, accumulated deficit $41.3 billion. Starlink: 10.3 million subscribers (doubled YoY), >2/3 of revenue, $1.2B segment profit in most recent quarter. Musk holds ~42% economic equity and 79–85% voting control via dual-class Class B shares. Anthropic pays SpaceX $1.25 billion/month through 2029 for Colossus cloud compute. Target raise: $75–80B at $1.75–2.0T implied valuation; IPO pricing June 18–30. On May 21, SpaceX completed its 60th orbital mission of 2026 (Starlink 29-sat, B1077 28th flight, 613th cumulative booster landing) at 10:04 UTC, ahead of the Starship IFT-12 Block 3 launch window opening at 22:30 UTC tonight from OLP-2, Starbase. IFT-12 objectives: Booster 19 (33 Raptor 3 engines) Gulf of Mexico splashdown, Ship 39 V3 (124.4 m) Indian Ocean splashdown, 20 Starlink mass-simulators + 2 heat-shield observer satellites. 55% favorable weather. SpaceX: 60 orbital missions in 2026, 613 total booster recoveries, 10,427+ Starlink satellites in orbit.
